body:
incident-bot: Pager alert: inference-serving-prod – elevated 5xx error rate detected (12% error rate over 5m, threshold 2%)
incident-bot: Severity: P2 · Runbook: /runbooks/inference/5xx-spike · Pager: @alice (oncall)

alice (oncall): ack'd the pager, jumping in now. starting with logs + metrics.
alice (oncall): creating war room -> https://meet.example.com/room/inference-3070012345 (prod incident)

bob (sre): on the war room. checking cluster autoscaler and GPU pool. any recent deploys?
carol (product): heads-up from product: we're seeing increased customer reports for streaming timeouts; possible user-facing impact for chat endpoints.
dave (support): received 3 tickets in the last 8 mins, all mention "response failed" or long spinning. I've escalated to oncall.

eva (eng-runtime): tailing the logs now. seeing repeated: `ERROR: kv-cache-miss -> fallback failed` and a bunch of `grpc: code = Internal` spikes. dumping a quick sample:```
2026-03-15T14:02:23Z inference-node-12 service: inference-serving pid=4321 ERROR kv-cache-miss key=conv_abc123
2026-03-15T14:02:24Z inference-node-12 service: inference-serving pid=4321 ERROR grpc: code = Internal desc=remote runtime error
```

alice (oncall): good catch. eva, can you check if the KV cache backend (redis-cluster-a) is healthy? also verify connection counts.
eva (eng-runtime): redis-cluster-a latency spiked to 120ms and started returning 500s around 14:00. nodes: redis-a1 high CPU, redis-a2 OOM-kill at 14:01 (see node events).

bob (sre): checking node events + autoscaler logs. looks like autoscaler trimmed pod count earlier due to a misinterpreted metric spike. might have removed a critical replica.

alice (oncall): owner assignment: alice = incident lead, eva = runtime lead, bob = infra lead, carol = communications liaison, dave = customer impact triage.
carol (product): for status page / external comms, draft below. feedback welcome: 

--- STATUS PAGE DRAFT ---
We are currently investigating elevated error rates affecting inference responses for a subset of customers in the us-west region. Some requests to the streaming/chat endpoints may fail or timeout. Our engineering team is actively mitigating the issue.
Impact: Partial degradation for streaming/chat endpoints in us-west.
ETA next update: 15 minutes.
--- END DRAFT ---

alice (oncall): +1. allocate 15m for initial update. carol, can you post that to status.redwood.com once we have confirmation on the root cause? mark it as "Investigating".

frank (ops-bot): Reminder: please confirm PagerDuty incident number when you acknowledge. Use `/pd incident create` if missing.
alice (oncall): PD-78921 created and acknowledged. linking to thread.

bob (sre): mitigation plan draft: 1) prevent further autoscaler activity for service by toggling `scale-lock` on the deployment, 2) restart redis-a2 after retrieving diagnostics, 3) scale inference-serving deployment to +30% capacity in us-west (manual to avoid autoscaler churn), 4) enable fallback model variant with local KV bypass for degraded paths.
eva (eng-runtime): I can run steps 2 and 3. will coordinate restart with infra to avoid thundering herd. switching to bypass may increase cost but should reduce 5xx.

alice (oncall): do it. bob, please apply `kubectl annotate deploy/inference-serving scale-lock=true --overwrite` and confirm.
bob (sre): applied `scale-lock` annotation. running `kubectl scale --replicas=20 deploy/inference-serving -n prod-us-west` now.

bob (sre): scaling action completed. new pod count: 20 -> observed CPU stable.
eva (eng-runtime): restarted redis-a2 with `systemctl restart redis` after collecting logs. redis-a2 journal shows OOM from previous cron job; cleared and memory now stable. latency dropping to ~25ms.

alice (oncall): monitoring metrics. 5xx now down from 12% -> 3.5% over last 5m. not fully healed but trending down.

carol (product): preparing customer notification template for impacted customers. draft: 

--- CUSTOMER NOTICE DRAFT ---
Subject: Brief service disruption affecting inference responses
Hi <Customer Name>,
We detected a service disruption impacting inference responses in us-west between 14:00–14:15 UTC. Some requests experienced failures or timeouts. Our engineers identified and mitigated an underlying cache backend issue and restarted affected services.
Current status: Partial recovery — most requests are succeeding; we continue to monitor.
If you see persistent errors, please reply to this message and include request IDs if available.
We apologize for the interruption.
— Redwood Inference Support
--- END DRAFT ---

dave (support): will send templated notice to customers with affected orgIDs once we reach stable <1% errors for 10m.

alice (oncall): ops checklist: add RCA channel, start evidence collection (logs, metrics, redis exports), and set follow-up postmortem owner.
eva (eng-runtime): exporting redis AOF snippet and config diff. attaching to the incident workspace.

frank (ops-bot): automations: creating incident tracker JIRA INF-2026-3070012345 and attaching PD-78921.

alice (oncall): quick note: don't post internal runbook commands in public customer replies. use sanitized logs only.

bob (sre): 5xx down to 1.2% over 5m, tailing at ~0.8% now. continuing to watch for 20m.
alice (oncall): last update: will send status page update now (Investigating -> Identified cause & Mitigation in progress). carol, please post the status page and customer notices per the plan. timestamp update + link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INF-3070012345

carol (product): posted status page update and queued customer emails to impacted orgIDs via support portal. copied notices to #customer-comms for review. :white_check_mark:

alice (oncall): oncall handoff note: if this persists past 16:00 UTC, escalate to on-call manager and open full postmortem. next update in 15m unless things regress.

frank (ops-bot): incident auto-runbook reminder: ensure `mitigation_success` checkbox checked when below 1% 5xx for 10m.

alice (oncall): thanks everyone. closing war room in 30m if metrics remain stable.

(reacts: :thumbsup: bob, :eyes: carol, :rocket: eva)
